findings.title: Borrowed structref ref leaks (and result is silently wrong) if an impl raises inside a @cfunc-wrapped callback
findings.category: NRT refcount leak across a raising call / swallowed exception
findings.description: None of the five @cfunc-wrapped @njit impls (_irr_update_impl/_combine_impl/_finalize_impl, plus init/destroy) wraps its body in a try/except. Per the documented numba @cfunc contract (MEMORY 'numba @cfunc swallows exceptions'), a raise inside an impl called from a @cfunc returns the zero/void default with no unwind to DuckDB (silent wrong result) AND leaks any NRT ref held across the raising call. update/combine/finalize each hold a live borrowed structref (borrow_structref, lines 156, 178-179, 201) at the moment they call vector_push (157-158) / vector_extend (180-181) / irr_bisect (206). vector_push/vector_extend call numpy.empty (numbox vector.py), which raises MemoryError on allocation failure; on that raise the borrowed structref's scope-exit decref is skipped, so the +1 from borrow_structref leaks, and DuckDB continues as though the row/group succeeded. The only realistic trigger is OOM during vector growth, so this is a latent hazard rather than a happy-path bug; but it is the exact failure mode called out in the review focus.
findings.impact: On an allocation failure during vector growth, a borrowed structref meminfo is leaked (NRT alloc!=free) and DuckDB silently proceeds with a partial/incorrect aggregate; the exception never reaches SQL. Undetectable except by the end-of-run leak assertion, which itself only runs after a successful query.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each impl body in a bare try/except that swallows-and-signals (or at minimum releases the borrowed ref) so a raise cannot both leak the ref and be silently discarded; e.g. compute results under try/except and, on failure, write NaN / set an error flag. Bare try/except (not try/finally, which re-raises on 0.65.1) both prevents the leak and makes the failure observable.

notes: Refcount ladder is balanced on the happy path and no hard memory defect was found. Verified: export_meminfo (+1) at init writes the meminfo intp into slot[0] (line 119) after the local structref is constructed with refcount 1; the local's scope-exit decref leaves the slot owning refcount 1 (cashflows/periods vectors each owned at refcount 1 by the structref). borrow_structref is net-0 in update/combine/finalize (entry incref balanced by scope-exit decref). release_meminfo (-1) in destroy (line 220) drives refcount to 0 and fires the imp_dtor cascade that frees the two Float64Vectors. Double-free across combine: NOT present -- vector_extend (line 180-181) copies src's buffer into tgt (numpy slice assignment), it does not transfer ownership; source states are destroyed independently by DuckDB, and DuckDB never passes the same pointer as source and target, so no aliasing. Slot decode (state_size=8, carray length-1 of intp per slot) is 64-bit-correct. finalize out_vals sized offset+count and written at offset+i is in-bounds under DuckDB's finalize contract (result vector capacity >= offset+count). Validity handling in update (val != 0 guard before duckdb_validity_row_is_valid) is correct. COMBINE-COVERAGE QUESTION: the leak test DOES exercise combine. DuckDB's physical aggregate operators (PhysicalUngroupedAggregate for Test 1/3, PhysicalHashAggregate for the GROUP BY in Test 2) route through the universal sink->combine->finalize path and call the combine callback to merge each thread-local aggregate state into the global state even when running single-threaded on tiny (<=18-row) tables; so the end-of-run alloc==free assertion (lines 372-377) covers the combine callback's refcount balance, not just init/update/finalize/destroy. (This is the one point I could not fully verify without running DuckDB; if in a given version an ungrouped single-thread aggregate short-circuits combine, coverage of the combine path would be lost, but combine itself is refcount-balanced regardless.)
